slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: In alkaline solution magnesium forms a coloured complex with Magon sulfonate (xylidyl blue); the colour intensity is proportional to the magnesium concentration.
Magnesium is the second most abundant intracellular cation after potassium; a cofactor of all ATP-dependent enzyme reactions.
Low magnesium: malabsorption, diuretic or aminoglycoside therapy; high: uraemia, chronic renal failure and others.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Magnesium Xylidyl” kit (IFU BSIS79-I, 08/11/22). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or heparinised plasma free of haemolysis, separated from the cells quickly; do not use oxalate or EDTA; stable 7 days at 2–8 °C.
Urine: acidify to pH 1 with HCl; warm cloudy urine to 60 °C for 10 min; dilute 1/10 and multiply the result by 10; 3 days at 2–8 °C.
Reagent: xylidyl blue 0.1 mmol/L, thioglycolic acid 0.7 mmol/L, DMSO 3000 mmol/L. Standard: magnesium 2 mg/dL.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 546 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes; disposable ware is recommended.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The reagent and standard are ready to use.
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light. Signs of deterioration: particles, colour change, turbidity or blank absorbance at 546 nm ≥ 1.8.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Use disposable ware to avoid magnesium contamination; glassware must be specially cleaned as the IFU describes, rinsed with distilled water and dried.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The values come from the SPINREACT “Magnesium Xylidyl” IFU (BSIS79-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 546 nm; temperature 37 °C or 15–25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — reagent 1.0 mL; standard — reagent 1.0 mL + standard 10 µL; sample — reagent 1.0 mL + sample 10 µL.
4. Mix and incubate: 5 min at room temperature or 3 min at 37 °C.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the absorbance (A) of the sample and standard against the blank; the colour is stable for at least 30 minutes.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: magnesium programme
rows: 3 min at 37 °C or 5 min at room temperature
Sample and standard — against the reagent blank

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Result (mg/dL) = (A sample − A blank) / (A standard − A blank) × 2 (standard concentration).
Conversion: mg/dL × 0.412 = mmol/L.
Linear up to 6 mg/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: IFU reference: serum/plasma 1.6–2.5 mg/dL (≈ 0.66–1.03 mmol/L); urine 24–244 mg/24 h.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Haemolysis and anticoagulants other than heparin interfere.
Magnesium contamination from glassware gives falsely high results — disposable ware is preferred.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Reagent: H318 — causes serious eye damage; wear goggles.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
